assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, the incretin effect and its pharmacological exploitation have produced a new therapeutic class that transformed type 2 diabetes treatment and obesity medicine, with cardiovascular and renal benefits now documented. The discovery chain is clear and the impact is very large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Holst (proglucagon processing, active GLP-1 forms and physiology), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, intestinotrophic GLP-2 and translation) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide) are the most defensible trio from the supplied names. Knudsen's medicinal-chemistry work on long-acting analogues is also major, and the credit allocation between peptide identification and drug development is unresolved; I have not verified the priority disputes independently.
assessment.maturity: Decades of clinical confirmation, multiple approved drugs, large outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Holst, Drucker, Mojsov, Knudsen and others not on the list is contested.
Whether a prize should honour basic physiology or drug development is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells created a new modality of cancer treatment with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and a growing list of approved products, and have opened applications beyond oncology. Conceptually original and clinically decisive.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR with 4-1BB costimulation) and Sadelain (CD28-costimulated CARs and preclinical proof of principle) are the clearest pairing. Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early CAR trials, but the decisive CAR contributions are less clearly his; the original CAR concept by others such as Eshhar is not within the supplied credited names, which limits a fully fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and long-term follow-up; remaining questions of toxicity, solid tumours and durability, but the core discovery is firmly established.
uncertainties: The supplied credit omits the originator of the chimeric receptor concept, so a fair configuration may be incomplete.
Long-term safety and secondary malignancy data are still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and its successors established the paradigm of rationally targeted therapy against a defined oncogenic kinase, turning chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal into a chronically manageable disease. The conceptual and clinical impact is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound programme and kinase inhibitor concept), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof of selectivity, trial leadership) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. The earlier discovery of BCR-ABL itself, as distinct from its inhibition, may be considered prior recognition or needed context; I am uncertain how that bears on allocation.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of survival data and independent confirmation; clearly mature.
uncertainties: Roles of the chemistry team (Zimmermann, not listed) versus clinical investigators may complicate credit.
Prior prizes in the BCR-ABL area may affect how a committee views novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with light, and has become a standard method across systems neuroscience with growing translational examples such as vision restoration. Discovery and tool development are both of high originality and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Six credited names make attribution hard. Nagel and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin identification and characterisation, with Bamberg) provide the molecular foundation, and Deisseroth (neuronal expression, tool development and widespread application) provides the decisive demonstration; Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck also made major contributions. I choose this trio as a plausible but contestable configuration.
assessment.maturity: Over a decade of independent use and replication; widely adopted. Timing is mature, though clinical validation is limited.
uncertainties: Choice among six credited contributors is genuinely unresolved and any trio excludes major contributors.
A methods-and-tools prize may be weighed against discoveries about disease mechanism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Clevers' identification of Lgr5 stem cells and the derivation of long-lived self-renewing epithelial organoids created a widely used experimental system for tissue biology, disease modelling, drug testing and personalised medicine. It is an original, clear and broadly adopted advance.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the central figure for stem-cell identity and the organoid concept, with Sato as first author of the key organoid papers. The supplied credit supports a clean one-to-two person configuration; other organoid pioneers outside the list may be relevant and I cannot verify that.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across laboratories and tissues, with extensive downstream use; mature, though clinical impact is still emerging.
uncertainties: The extent of clinical translation remains modest.
Relative standing against other stem-cell and organoid work is uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, dramatically altering a previously lethal childhood disease. It combines mechanistic RNA biology with striking clinical benefit and a platform effect for splice-switching oligonucleotides.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and identification of the intronic silencer targeted) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) form a compact and fair pair. Other contributors in SMN gene discovery and trials are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up and independent confirmation; strong, but still relatively recent for recognition.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently foundational versus applied.
Place of SMN1 gene discovery and gene therapy in the same story is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis changed the treatment of chronic inflammatory disease, with anti-TNF biologics used across rheumatology, gastroenterology and dermatology. A clear, original concept with enormous clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly developed the TNF-dependence concept and led the first clinical trials, a clean pair. Contributions from cytokine cloning and antibody engineering by others may be seen as part of the story, but the supplied credit supports the pair.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experience and independent confirmation; fully mature, and arguably late in recognition.
uncertainties: Prior Lasker recognition and the breadth of other contributors to TNF biology could complicate a narrow configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cell survival, not only proliferation, drives cancer, defined the apoptotic regulatory family, and led to venetoclax. A deep and clear conceptual advance with lasting translational impact.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the Melbourne work establishing the BCL-2 family and its role in lymphoma, and Vaux showed the survival function in vivo. Strasser is a major contributor but a trio must exclude one of four; earlier translocation discovery and the C. elegans cell-death prior prize (2002) bear on allocation, and I am unsure of the precise priority.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by independent work and approved drugs; mature. Overlap with the 2002 prize may reduce perceived novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier apoptosis prize is unresolved.
Choosing three of four credited contributors is contestable.
